'''Siward Cass''' was a [[Human/Legends|Human]] [[Gender/Legends|male]] [[Imperial officer/Legends|military officer]] who served the [[Galactic Empire/Legends|Galactic Empire]] aboard the [[DS-1 Orbital Battle Station/Legends|first Death Star]] during the [[Galactic Civil War/Legends|Galactic Civil War]]. By [[0 BBY/Legends|0 BBY]], he was a war veteran and had acted as an [[Aide/Legends|aide]] to [[Grand Moff/Legends|Grand Moff]] [[Wilhuff Tarkin/Legends|Wilhuff Tarkin]] for many [[Standard year/Legends|years]].

==Biography==
{{Quote|Yes.|Wilhuff Tarkin to Cass|<ref name="anh" />}}
A [[Human/Legends|Human]] [[Gender/Legends|male]], Siward Cass was [[Reproduction/Legends|born]] in the [[Patriim system/Legends|Patriim system]],<ref name="SWI" /><ref name="Twit" /> within the [[Seswenna sector/Legends|Seswenna sector]] of the [[Outer Rim Territories/Legends|Outer Rim]] region of [[The galaxy/Legends|the galaxy]].<ref name="EAOC">{{SW|url=news/star-wars-the-essential-atlas-online-companion|text=''Star Wars: The Essential Atlas'' Online Companion|int=Star Wars: The Essential Atlas Online Companion}}</ref> At some point during his life, he joined the [[Imperial Army/Legends|ground forces]] of [[Palpatine/Legends|Palpatine's]] [[Galactic Empire/Legends|Galactic Empire]]. For many [[Standard year/Legends|years]], he served as an [[Aide/Legends|aide]] to [[Wilhuff Tarkin/Legends|Wilhuff Tarkin]], [[Grand Moff/Legends|Grand Moff]] of the [[Oversector Outer]].

By the [[Time/Legends|time]] of the [[Galactic Civil War/Legends|Galactic Civil War]], a major galactic conflict fought between the Empire and the [[Alliance to Restore the Republic/Legends|Rebel Alliance]], he was considered a veteran. Cass acted as the [[Chief/Legends|chief]] communications officer aboard the [[DS-1 Orbital Battle Station/Legends|first]] [[Death Star/Legends|Death Star]] [[Battle station/Legends|battle station]]. He was entrusted with extremely sensitive information and communications between Tarkin and the Imperial government. Because of this, he was part of the Death Star command, and had a seat at its [[Death Star conference room/Legends|conference table]]. Cass' duties ranged from handling routine communications to delivering priority news to the Grand Moff.<ref name="SWI" />

In [[0 BBY/Legends|0 BBY]], the Imperials managed to capture [[Princess/Legends|Princess]] [[Leia Organa Solo/Legends|Leia Organa]] of [[Alderaan/Legends|Alderaan]], who had strong ties with the Rebel Alliance, and Tarkin tried to make her confess the location of the Rebels' headquarters. Organa ended up giving the name of [[Dantooine/Legends|Dantooine]], after which that planet was checked for Rebel presence. Subsequently, Cass was committed with the delicate task of reporting to Tarkin that it no longer held any active base. Although he found the situation uncomfortable,<ref name="ANHn">[[Star Wars: A New Hope (novelization)|''Star Wars Episode IV: A New Hope'' novel]]</ref> Cass did his duty with no signs of nervousness. Having made his report, he immediately exited the room.<ref name="anh" /> Cass perished as the Death Star was destroyed during the [[Battle of Yavin/Legends|Battle of Yavin]].<ref name="Chrome Perspectives" />

==Personality and traits==
Around the Battle of Yavin, Siward Cass was a pale-skinned, older man who sported short gray [[Hair/Legends|hair]].<ref name="anh" /> Within the Imperial military, he was considered a model adjutant. However, despite his reputation for being self-possessed and discreet,<ref name="SWI" /> Cass still was wary of Tarkin's wrath, and he disliked being the one bearing bad news to the Moff.<ref name="ANHn" />

==Behind the scenes==
Siward Cass made his first appearance in the [[1977]] [[Star Wars: Episode IV A New Hope|''Star Wars'': Episode IV ''A New Hope'']], in which he was portrayed by English actor [[Patrick Jordan]]. Albeit unnamed in the movie itself,<ref name="anh" /> he was referred to as "Cass" in its [[Star Wars: A New Hope (novelization)|novelization]].<ref name="ANHn" /> Jordan got the part of Cass in ''A New Hope'' through his friendship with [[Alec Guinness]], who portrayed [[Obi-Wan Kenobi/Legends|Obi-Wan Kenobi]] and whom had worked with Jordan for [[Wikipedia:The Old Vic|The Old Vic]] company in the [[1940s]]. However, Jordan shared Guinness' contempt for the film, dubious about the film's prospects.<ref>{{WebCite|Date=2020-02-10|url=https://www.theguardian.com/tv-and-radio/2020/feb/10/patrick-jordan-obituary|text=Patrick Jordan obituary|author=Weaver, Matthew|archivedate=20200213104356}}</ref>

[[File:Cabadge.jpg|thumb|right|180px|Cass's rank insignia.]]
Although Cass was sometimes identified as a [[General/Legends|general]] by fan-created sources,<ref name="theforce">{{WebCite|url=http://theforce.net/swtc/insignia/badges.html#mjgeneral|text=theforce.net|archivedate=20011109130830}}</ref> he was initially only referred to in [[canon]] as "Imperial Officer Cass" or "Officer Cass," and his exact rank long remained unknown. Unlike most characters whose names are known in the script, Officer Cass did not have an entry in the [[StarWars.com]] official [[Databank (original)|Databank]].

In [[2013]], Cass was eventually given the first name "Siward" and the rank of "Chief" in both the ''[[Death Star Owner's Technical Manual]]''<ref name="DSOTM">''[[Death Star Owner's Technical Manual]]''</ref> and the article [[A Certain Point of View (department)|''The Death Star Coup'']], written by [[Jason Fry]] for the [[Star Wars Insider Special Edition 2014|Special Edition 2014]] of the ''[[Star Wars Insider]]'' magazine.<ref name="SWI" /> According to [[Chris Trevas]], one of the co-authors of the ''Technical Manual'', Cass was given that rank because his insignia plaque was the same one as [[Moradmin Bast/Legends|Moradmin Bast's]],<ref name="Siward Cass's rank">{{Facebook|username=StarWarsSourcebooks|url=StarWarsSourcebooks/posts/634665586583552|name=Chris Trevas|date=30-10-2013|quote=Cass is now labeled Chief since his rank badge matches Bast's. Jason's Insider article may have more info.|archivedate=20200820185325}}</ref> who was first identified as "Chief Bast" in the [[Star Wars Customizable Card Game|''Star Wars'' Customizable Card Game]] [[Premiere Limited]] expansion set.<ref name="ccg">{{CCG|set=Premiere Limited|cardname=Chief Bast}}</ref> Fry chose the character's first name as a nod to [[Wikipedia:William Shakespeare|William Shakespeare's]] play [[Wikipedia:Macbeth|''Macbeth'']], which featured the character of [[Wikipedia:Siward, Earl of Northumbria|Siward, Earl of Northumberland]], general of the English forces.<ref name="Twit2">{{Twitter|jasoncfry|status/396712749956218880|[[Jason Fry]]|nobackup=1}}</ref>

In the [[1981]] [[Star Wars (radio)|radio]] episode "[[Death Star's Transit]]," Cass's line is delivered instead by [[Conan Antonio Motti/Legends|Motti]].<ref name="Death Star's Transit">{{SWRadio|Death Star's Transit}}</ref> The [[2008]] novel [[Death Star (novel)|''Death Star'']] features an unidentified [[Colonel/Legends|colonel]] serving as Tarkin's aide, although it is not clear whether he is intended to be Cass or not.<ref name="ds">[[Death Star (novel)|''Death Star'']]</ref>
